name: Kentucky

office.name: Kentucky Transportation Cabinet - Division of Motor Carriers, Overweight/Over-Dimensional Permits

fees.note: Single trip OW/OD permit $60 per KYTC (plus 4% card or $3 ACH processing fee), valid 10 days. KRS 189.270 (as amended eff. July 15, 2026) now leaves fees to regulation, and a proposed 601 KAR 1:018 amendment filed Sept 15, 2026 sets single trip at $120 - verify which fee is in force.

Loads above the routine permit maximums (7-axle combination 160,000 lb; 6-axle 120,000; 5-axle 96,000) need a route/bridge analysis by KYTC's Bridge Preservation Branch. The proposed 601 KAR 1:018 amendment adds a $500 superload bridge analysis fee.

restrictions.text: Travel allowed 24 hours, 7 days and no holiday restrictions unless the permit says otherwise (mobile homes: daylight Mon-Sat only, no Sunday).

No permitted travel 7-9 a.m. and 4-6 p.m. Mon-Fri in Boone, Kenton, Campbell, Fayette and Jefferson (Louisville) counties or on the Owensboro KY 2155 bridge; loads originating in Fayette County are exempt on I-64/I-75 and connecting routes within 3 miles.
Over 12' wide: no move when the National Weather Service has issued a wind advisory, or when weather/road conditions make the move dangerous.

notes: Escorts: 601 KAR 1:018 Section 14 sets the 2-lane / 4-lane rules (non_interstate modeled as 2-lane, interstate as 4-lane). KYTC's escort page adds 2 front + 2 rear over 16' wide, 1 front + 2 rear (with pivot/steerable dolly) over 120' long, and a rear escort when rear overhang exceeds 10'. Over 14'11" high the front escort runs a height pole. A trail escort is also required on 2-lane roads if the load cannot keep the posted speed.
Over 15'6" high: submit the OW/OD Proposed Route Survey (TC 95-625). Carrier must measure all clearances along the route.

Overweight permits require the power unit to be registered for at least 80,000 lb and at least 5 axles on combinations. Max permitted gross: 5 axles 96,000; 6 axles 120,000; 7 axles 160,000 lb; trunnion axles by bridge analysis. 'Superload' here = above 160,000 lb (Kentucky defines no superload class in the current regulation).
Front overhang on a combination vehicle is prohibited; rear overhang max 1/3 of trailer length (35' total).
Legal: 8'6" wide, 13'6" high, 53' semitrailer on interstates/designated highways; 8' wide and 65' overall on other state highways.
